guard.notes: Repo-level .codex/hooks.json registers a PreToolUse hook that runs the guard with AGENT_RUNTIME=codex and AGENT_RUNTIME_CONFIG=.agents/runtime/codex/config.json (exit 0 allows, exit 2 blocks). Schema (verified against codex-rs/config/src/hook_config.rs, 2026-09-30): the file is {"description"?, "hooks": {<Event>: [{"matcher"?, "hooks": [{"type":"command", "command", "timeout"(sec)?, "statusMessage"?}]}]}} - event names live inside the "hooks" wrapper, never at the top level (deny_unknown_fields); events: PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop, Interrupt. Codex loads project hooks only after the .codex/ layer is trusted via the /hooks command; until then the policy is honoured behaviourally - pipe a doubtful call through the guard before running it. Hooks run from the repository root, so the relative guard path works.

capabilitiesNotes: toolEvents: this file's own `guard.notes` already states the confirmed fact - "Codex CLI reads AGENTS.md natively but has no repository-level PreToolUse hook" - no tool-call event reaches this repository's policy or observability layer without a user mirroring config by hand outside the repo, matching `hooksSupport: behavioral`. The other five: no script, doc, event log or working integration in this repository exercises or confirms Codex subagent spawn, resume, cancel or usage reporting, or worktree awareness - general belief about the Codex product is not evidence this project has confirmed, so all four are left `unknown` rather than guessed. Updated 2026-09-30: Codex gained repo-level hooks and .codex/hooks.json now wires PreToolUse to the local guard, so toolEvents moves to `unknown` - it becomes `verified` at the first exercised run in this repository.

permissions.notes: Sandbox and approval policy live in the user's ~/.codex/config.toml, not in this repository. Structural changes to roles, agents or skills always need explicit user approval, in every mode.
